note: The BUDGET law of the `evaluate` capability. `⏯️preview-eval-run.json` says how the `previewEval` run schedules hops and what its abort releases; this says how a long operator's evaluation is CUT into interactive steps in the first place, so that there is a boundary for the abort — and for a liveness watchdog — to land on at all. Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language must fold these envelopes and answer the same outcomes, the same published status and the same continuation. ⛓️ 2026-09-14: three rows declared `phase: "idle", ratio: 1.0` while their own `owesHop` was TRUE — the defect written down. A surface that says `idle` for a window it knows owes another hop is the reason a whole 23 s evaluation published nothing to show (`📓️wgpu-progress-visibility-2026-09-14.md`). They now declare the chain phase. ⚠️ These rows drive a session with NO published node census (no `FlowHost` is synced), so the ratio they pin is the best a session without a denominator can give: `0.0` while working, never `1.0`. The census-present case — the monotone `n/m` a pill prints — is pinned by `a_live_evaluation_publishes_non_idle_frames_with_a_monotone_ratio_and_an_offered_abort` and by the shared `🛑️surface-controls/🔣️.json` `progressTimeline` rows both renderers answer.

laws.oneRequestOneStep: An `evaluate` request is answered within the requester's own wall allowance, ALWAYS. An operator that cannot finish inside it answers `done: false` with its progress; the run's next hop re-emits the IDENTICAL request and the extension resumes the job it parked under the same `nodeHash`. This is the same resumption mechanism budgeted `tessellate` uses — no timers, no parked futures, because a plugin has nowhere to hold one.
laws.unbudgetedOperatorsAreUnchanged: An operator with no sub-structure completes inside the first round trip and its envelope is indistinguishable in latency from the one-shot call it replaces. Only an operator that offers a resumable job can ever answer `done: false`.
laws.progressIsMonotone: `unitsDone` never decreases across the round trips of one evaluation. `unitsTotal` is the plan known so far and may be revised UPWARD exactly once, when a stage that could only be planned after an earlier one ran finally reports its size.
laws.workingSeedsNothing: A working envelope seeds no node cache entry. Seeding a partial evaluation would publish a half-built solid as if it were the answer.
laws.workingIsInFlight: While an evaluation is working, the published status reports `inFlight >= 1`, a non-idle phase and a ratio below 1 — even though NO tessellation has been admitted. A preview that reports `idle` while its kernel is busy is the defect this fixture exists to forbid.
laws.cancelledOwesNothing: A cancelled envelope seeds nothing and gives its window up: whoever cancelled the kernel job owes nobody a continuation, and a hop here would restart the evaluation that was stopped.
laws.completeSeedsTheOutput: A complete envelope's `outputJson` is exactly the out dictionary the unbudgeted evaluation would have produced — a stepped answer and a one-shot answer are indistinguishable downstream, including the `{"error": …}` body a refused evaluation carries.
laws.anUnknownPhaseIsComputing: A phase tag the surface's vocabulary does not know reads as `computing`, never as `idle`: the envelope that carried it said the job is still working.
laws.aBareDictionaryIsAFinishedEvaluation: A response body that is not an envelope at all is read as a finished evaluation whose output IS that body. It is the only reading that cannot lose an answer.
laws.theBudgetKeepsTheWorkerAlive: The wall allowance is chosen below the host's shard liveness window, not merely below its termination threshold: a guest turn that never yields blocks the worker's event loop and its progress ticker with it, so a long turn and a dead worker are indistinguishable to the host. Returning between steps is what makes them distinguishable.
laws.answersArmNothing: A fold never DISPATCHES a hop. It settles the window's outstanding answer and leaves the window owing a hop exactly when the evaluation continues. What it may do — and now does — is RUN that owed hop itself, inline, inside the answer's own guest turn: the answer routes are addressed at the same preview window the hop is, so the fold already holds the retained session, the document, the config and that window's transient. The admission question is the run job's own scheduling question, so the chain's shape cannot change; only who runs the hop. A fold that declines leaves the latch untouched and the run job dispatches the round trip exactly as before.

rows.why: The headline case: a boolean that spent its wall allowance inside the validation stage.
A future operator's own vocabulary must never be published as `idle`.
The terminal case: the job finished inside this round trip. A window that still OWES a hop is not idle and is certainly not complete: the round trip ended, the evaluation did not.

The error body travels inside the output exactly as an unbudgeted refusal always did. A window that still OWES a hop is not idle and is certainly not complete: the round trip ended, the evaluation did not.
The gesture already stopped the chain; this answer only observes it.

An answer that predates the envelope contract must still be an answer, never a lost one. A window that still OWES a hop is not idle and is certainly not complete: the round trip ended, the evaluation did not.

steppedOperator.why: The one operator family measured long enough to trip the host's 16 s shard watchdog inside a single turn: `🍩️sphere-cut-with-torus` costs 4.5 s of exact boolean natively (1.5 s of it stitching, 3.0 s validating) and over 16 s in the served wasm.
steppedOperator.steppedEqualsOneShot: Driving the job one unit at a time must produce the SAME out dictionary as the one-shot evaluation of the same input. The stepped path IS the algorithm; there is no second implementation to drift from.
steppedOperator.cancelMidWay: Cancelling between steps terminates the job with phase `cancelled`; a job that already produced its output is never retired by a later cancel.

inlineContinuation.why: The last removable round trip of the preview chain. After wave coalescing every example still paid one `flowEvalResolve` -> `flowEvalTick` pair per dependency LEVEL — 1 391 ms apiece on React (`react-hop-latency-2026-09-14.md` section 2.1). The pair exists only because the fold and the hop used to live on different routes. They do not any more.
inlineContinuation.owningPublicationLayer: `flowEvalTick`, `flowEvalResolve` and `flowTessellateResolve` are ONE window-addressed work with ONE publication lane (`WindowTransient`). A continuation that advanced the chain without publishing would buy hops by going blind, and intermediate geometry plus the monotone status pill are exactly what a user cancels out of. `flowEvalRelease` and `flowTessellateCancelResolve` stay off that layer: they address an extension actor, not a window, and must still reach it once the window is gone.

admission.owedHopOnly: A fold may only take over a hop the scheduler would have dispatched — the window owes one, nothing is armed, and no sibling answer of its wave is still in flight. It may never invent a hop.
admission.neverResumesACancelledChain: A cancelled session refuses every continuation. Beginning a tick retires the cancelled banner, so a continuation on a cancelled chain would un-cancel the run the user stopped.
admission.oneTurnOneDeadline: Every dag walk of one guest turn shares ONE wall deadline. An inline walk inherits the turn's deadline instead of opening a fresh allowance, which is what stops a chained continuation from stretching the interactive hold one ceiling per wave.
admission.aSpentTurnParks: A turn with less than the reserve of its evaluation allowance left runs no further walk. Park is not a state — it is the absence of the continuation: the latch is untouched and the run job dispatches the round trip.
admission.oneWavePerTurn: A continuation that parks extension work stops there. The answers have to cross to the host before the next wave can be walked at all, so one turn can never run two waves of the same chain.

inlineContinuation.statusStillAdvancesPerWave: The census the status pill prints is published by the walk, so it advances once per WAVE exactly as it did when each wave cost a hop. The user sees the same monotone sequence (`preview-cancel.json` chainCensus), sooner.
inlineContinuation.hopsPerExampleNote: `hops` is `flowEvalTick` actions the host dispatches for one cold-cache example load in the edit lane. `beforeCoalescing` is the measured u64-journey column of `react-perf-ceilings-audit-2026-09-14.md` section 1; `afterCoalescing` is the modelled levels+1 of `flow-tick-coalescing-2026-09-14.md` section 3; `afterInline` is 1 for every example, because the gesture arms the first hop and every wave after it runs inside an answer's own turn. Extra hops are possible and are each a declined continuation.

rows.why: The affordance the whole publication argument exists for: a gesture landing between two waves must still stop the chain, and every answer already crossing when it landed must continue nothing.
A wave whose turn has no wall left must hand the round trip back to the host rather than overrun the interactive hold.
Park is the absence of the continuation, never a state of its own: a one-wave chain whose terminal walk is refused leaves the window owing exactly the hop it owed, and the run job dispatches it.

inlineContinuation.hopLadder: One chain of N waves is N+1 hops: one per wave plus a terminal walk that owes nothing and records the window finished. With the continuation admitted throughout, hop 1 is dispatched by the host and hops 2..N+1 all run inline, so `afterInline` is 1 and the inline-wave count is N. Each declined continuation moves exactly one hop back to the host.
inlineContinuation.hopIndexing: `cancelBeforeHop` / `spentTurnBeforeHop` are 1-based positions in the hop ladder. Hop 1 is always the one the host dispatches; hop i+1 is the walk the last answer of wave i unblocks; hop N+1 is the terminal walk that owes nothing. Naming hop i means the interference lands in the guest turn that would have run hop i inline.
